passages.heading: Debt note
passages.text: 5. DEBT OBLIGATIONS ​ Long-term debt consists of: ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ January 31, ​ February 1, ​ ​ ​ ​ 2026 ​ ​ ​ 2025 1.70 % to 8.00 % Senior Notes due through 2064 ​ $ 14,864 ​ $ 14,854 Other ​ 1,011 ​ 1,055 ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Total debt, excluding obligations under finance leases ​ 15,875 ​ 15,909 Less current portion ​ ( 1,366 ) ​ ( 104 ) ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Total long-term debt, excluding obligations under finance leases ​ $ 14,509 ​ $ 15,805 ​ In 2024, the Company issued $ 10,500 of senior notes to pay a portion of the cash consideration for its proposed merger with Albertsons and general corporate purposes. The Company repaid certain senior notes of $ 4,700 that were subject to a special mandatory redemption due to the termination of the merger. See Note 18 for additional information related to these issuances and repayments. ​ On September 13, 2024, the Company entered into an unsecured revolving credit facility (the “Credit Agreement”), with a termination date of September 13, 2029, unless extended as permitted under the Credit Agreement. The Credit Agreement amended the agreement governing the Company’s $ 2,750 credit facility that would otherwise have terminated on July 6, 2026. Under the Credit Agreement, the aggregate amount of initial commitments under the revolving credit facility is $ 2,750 , which could have been increased by $ 2,250 to $ 5,000 upon the closing date of the proposed merger with Albertsons (such additional commitments, the “Albertsons Closing Date Additional Commitments”). Concurrently with the termination of the merger agreement (the “Merger Agreement”) with Albertsons on December 11, 2024, the Albertsons Closing Date Additional Commitments were automatically terminated in accordance with the terms of the Credit Agreement. On and after December 11, 2024, the amount of outstanding commitments under the Credit Agreement is $ 2,750 . ​ Borrowings under the Credit Agreement bear interest, at the Company’s option, at either (i) adjusted Term Secured Overnight Financing Rate (“SOFR”) plus a market spread, based on the Company’s Public Debt Rating or (ii) the base rate, defined as the highest of (a) the Federal Funds Rate plus 0.5 %, (b) Wells Fargo’s prime rate , and (c) one month Term SOFR plus 1.0 %, plus a market rate spread based on the Company’s Public Debt Rating . The Company will also pay a Commitment Fee based on its Public Debt Rating and Letter of Credit fees equal to a market rate spread based on the Company’s Public Debt Rating. “Public Debt Rating” means, as of any date, the rating that has been most recently announced by either S&P or Moody’s, as the case may be, for any class of non-credit enhanced long-term senior unsecured debt issued by the Company. ​ The Credit Agreement contains a covenant, which, among other things, requires the maintenance of a leverage ratio of not greater than 3.50 :1.00. The Company may repay the Credit Agreement in whole or in part at any time without premium or penalty. The Credit Agreement is not guaranteed by the Company’s subsidiaries. ​

passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: RESULTS OF OPERATIONS. ​ The following discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations of The Kroger Co. should be read in conjunction with the “Forward-looking Statements” section set forth in Part I and the “Risk Factors” section set forth in Item 1A of Part I of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. MD&A is provided as a supplement to, and should be read in conjunction with, our Consolidated Financial Statements and the accompanying notes thereto contained in Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K, as well as Part II, Item 7 “Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended February 1, 2025, which provides additional information on comparisons of fiscal years 2024 and 2023. ​ OUR VALUE CREATION MODEL – DELIVERING CONSISTENT AND ATTRACTIVE TOTAL SHAREHOLDER RETURN ​ Kroger’s proven value creation model is allowing us to deliver today and invest for the future. The foundation of our value creation model is our omnichannel retail business, including fuel and health and wellness. By executing on our go-to-market strategy built on Fresh, Our Brands , Personalization and eCommerce, we are creating a shopping experience that builds loyalty and grows sales. Our retail business generates traffic and data which accelerates growth in our high operating margin alternative profit businesses, like retail media. In turn, the value generated from these businesses enables us to reinvest back into our retail business. ​ We are focused on our top priorities and delivering an exceptional customer experience to accelerate this flywheel effect. By expanding our store network and improving our eCommerce capabilities, we expect to grow households and increase sales. Our model provides various ways to generate net earnings growth. ​ We believe this will be achieved by: ​ ● Growing identical sales without fuel. Our plan involves maximizing growth opportunities in our retail business and is supported by continued strategic investments in our associates and greater value for our customers to ensure we deliver a full, fresh and friendly experience for every customer, every time. In an effort to serve more households, we plan to invest in major storing projects that allow us to increase both in-store and eCommerce sales. As more and more customers incorporate eCommerce into their permanent routines, we expect eCommerce sales to grow at a double-digit rate – a faster pace than other food at home sales – over time; and ​ ● Expanding operating margin through long-term initiatives in gross margin, growing alternative profit businesses and productivity and cost savings initiatives that are focused on simplifying our business and modernizing our ways of working. Together, we expect these will enable us to improve operating margin, while balancing strategic price investments for customers and investments in associates to improve customer experience. ​ We expect to continue to generate strong free cash flow and are committed to being disciplined with capital deployment in support of our value creation model and stated capital allocation priorities. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow comfortably exceeds capital spending plus dividends, and also covers buybacks, so internally generated funds finance the store and eCommerce investment programme without incremental borrowing. Cash conversion is the strongest element of the profile and compares favourably with the sector median on cash flow to debt.

Cash flow to debt sits above the sector median and improved year on year, reflecting steady grocery cash generation from the omnichannel and alternative profit businesses. This supports the top-tier cash-flow risk band and gives meaningful headroom before the next threshold, although a modest decline in operating cash flow would narrow it.

key_risks.text: Gross leverage rose year on year and now sits above the sector median, while net leverage is only marginally above the peer median. The increase reflects debt raised for the terminated Albertsons merger, so the balance sheet carries acquisition-related debt without the earnings that transaction would have delivered.

Interest coverage fell sharply year on year and is well below the sector median, with operating margin also far below peers. Thin grocery margins leave limited cushion: the disclosed risk factor notes that liquidity depends on financial market conditions and the ability to issue commercial paper at acceptable rates.

The debt note shows senior notes maturing through the mid-century, with the current portion rising sharply year on year and a large bullet concentrated beyond year five. Refinancing that tower depends on maintaining investment-grade access, and the revolver is unsecured and not guaranteed by subsidiaries.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Free cash flow covers dividends several times over but falls just short of total dividends plus buybacks, so shareholder returns absorb essentially all discretionary cash and leave little retained for deleveraging. Capital spending is the largest single use and is expected to stay elevated as store and eCommerce investment continues.

The revolver covenant requires leverage no greater than three and a half times, and reported leverage sits below that test with room to absorb some EBITDA erosion. Coverage of interest from operating income remains adequate but thin relative to peers, so earnings volatility rather than liquidity is the binding constraint.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is intermediate, driven by leverage in the second tier while cash flow sits in the strongest tier. Leverage is above the sector median and has deteriorated year on year, but cash generation and free cash flow to debt compare well with peers, supporting a stable, investment-grade-like credit posture.

Our forward view is that deleveraging will be gradual: shareholder distributions consume nearly all free cash flow, and margin recovery is the main lever. A current ratio below one and below peers is typical for grocery and not a liquidity concern given revolver access, but sustained margin weakness would pressure coverage.

credit_strengths.text: 經營現金流穩健超過資本開支加股息，亦足以覆蓋回購，因此內部產生資金可為門店及電商投資計劃提供資金，而無需增量借貸。現金轉換是該信貸狀況最強的元素，並在現金流對債務比率上優於行業中位數。
現金流對債務比率高於行業中位數，並按年改善，反映全渠道及替代利潤業務帶來穩定的雜貨現金生成。這支持最高級別的現金流風險區間，並在下一門檻前提供有意義的緩衝，儘管經營現金流小幅下降會收窄該緩衝。

key_risks.text: 總槓桿按年上升，現時高於行業中位數，而淨槓桿僅略高於同業中位數。增幅反映為已終止的Albertsons合併而籌集的債務，因此資產負債表承擔與收購相關的債務，卻沒有該交易本應帶來的盈利。
利息覆蓋率按年大幅下降，並遠低於行業中位數，經營利潤率亦遠低於同業。微薄的雜貨利潤率留下有限緩衝：披露的風險因素指出，流動性取決於金融市場狀況及以可接受利率發行商業票據的能力。
債務附註顯示高級票據於本世紀中葉前到期，流動部分按年大幅上升，且大額子彈還款集中於五年之後。為該債務塔再融資取決於維持投資級別准入，而循環信貸為無抵押且未獲附屬公司擔保。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 自由現金流覆蓋股息數倍，但略低於股息加回購總額，因此股東回報基本上吸收所有可自由支配現金，留存作去槓桿的資金甚少。資本開支是最大的單一用途，並預期在門店及電商投資持續下保持高企。
循環信貸契約要求槓桿不超過三倍半，而報告槓桿低於該測試，並有空間吸收部分EBITDA侵蝕。經營利潤對利息的覆蓋仍然充足，但相對同業偏薄，因此制約因素在於盈利波動而非流動性。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為中間級別，由處於第二梯隊的槓桿驅動，而現金流則處於最強梯隊。槓桿高於行業中位數並按年惡化，但現金生成及自由現金流對債務比率與同業相比表現良好，支持穩定、類投資級別的信貸狀況。
我們的前瞻觀點是去槓桿將循序漸進：股東分派消耗幾乎所有自由現金流，而利潤率復甦是主要槓桿。流動比率低於一且低於同業，對雜貨業而言屬典型情況，鑑於循環信貸准入並不構成流動性憂慮，但持續的利潤率疲弱將對覆蓋率構成壓力。
